prompt: A storage box is $6 \times \frac{1}{2} \times 4$. Find its volume.
hint: The volume is the product of the three dimensions. Choose an order that saves the fraction for last.

hints.title: 🔁 Another angle
hints.text: Think of a full $6 \times 1 \times 4$ box with volume $24$. This storage box is only half as wide, so it holds half as much.
The volume is the product of the three dimensions. Choose an order that saves the fraction for last.
Multiply $6 \times 4 = 24$ first. Then multiply by $\frac{1}{2}$, which means taking half of $24$.
Half of $24$ is $12$, so the volume of the storage box is $12$ cubic units.

explanation: The volume of the box is $6 \times \frac{1}{2} \times 4$.
The order of multiplying does not matter, so do the whole numbers first: $6 \times 4 = 24$.
Multiplying by $\frac{1}{2}$ takes half of the number: $24 \times \frac{1}{2} = 12$.
The volume of the storage box is $12$ cubic units.
